To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the retention of CO2 in wheat bulks was poor, and that the retention was not affected by the mode of application, the point of introduction, the amount and the frequency of application, or the surface left uncovered or covered with PVDC.

CO2 distribution in the wheat bulks was affected by the point of application and mode of application of the dry ice; the retention efficiency of CO2 in bolted-metal bin was low; and the retention efficiency was affected by the amount and frequency at which dry ice was applied.
the distribution of introduced CO2 in wheat bulk is affected by the location of application and that the CO2 retention efficiency of the bin is generally low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to control insect pests in wheat in bolted-metal storage bins.
the development of a new method for the application of CO2 gas in bolted-metal bin storage systems.
the distribution and maintenance of CO2 gas in grain bulks contained in bins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aeration ducts are more effective in distributing and maintaining high concentrations of introduced CO2 than are perforated floors.
CO2 distribution is affected by aeration and the mode and point of application of dry-ice blocks.
the CO2 concentrations in a wheat bulk are affected by the method of application, the point of introduction, and the amount of CO2 applied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the distribution and retention of CO2 in bolted-metal grain bins can be significantly improved by placing insulated boxes filled with blocks of dry ice on the surface of the grain bulk, and by covering the grain surface with PVDC sheet.
CO2 distribution and retention in bolted-metal storage bins can be controlled by sealing the bin and applying dry ice at the top of the grain bulk.
the CO2 distribution and retention efficiency in bolted-metal grain bins can be improved by placing insulated boxes filled with solid CO2 blocks on the grain surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distribution of CO2 in wheat bulks can be controlled by the method of application and the amount of grain surface left exposed to the atmosphere.
the distribution and maintenance of CO2 in wheat bulks is influenced by many factors, and that the use of aeration ducts is not the only option.
CO2 gas can be used to control insects in wheat stored in bolted bins.
